subject: Capacity activation: staggered region rollout and burst sizing
messages:
From: Sara Malik <sara@helixai.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: infra@helixai.com
Date: 2027-05-16 09:12 -0700
Subject: HelixAI: initial capacity needs and rollout preferences

Thanks Jonas / Monica — great chatting earlier. Per our conversation, attaching a short traffic sample and a one-page sketch of our desired multipool shape. High level: we expect two steady-state frontends (text generation) with spikes on weekday mornings. Peak 99th percentile throughput target ~180 RPS across inference endpoints for v2.

Asks:
- Can Redwood provision a dedicated pool sized for 120 concurrent tokens-per-step workloads and a burst strategy to cover sudden 3x spikes?
- Preferred initial region is us-west-2 (customer proximity), with eu-west-1 for disaster/fallback.
- We're ok starting with a conservative burst cap and iterating (we want predictable pricing).

Attachments: helix_expected_traffic_q3.csv (CSV, 42KB), initial_multipool_sketch.pdf (PDF, 220KB)

Next step: would love a quick ops-oriented reply with staging region, recommended GPU family, and a proposed automaticscaling/burst policy we can review with infra and procurement.

—Sara Malik
Program Manager, HelixAI
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Malik <sara@helixai.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-16 11:03 -0700
Subject: Re: HelixAI: initial capacity needs and rollout preferences

Sara — thanks for the context and attachments. Quick internal read and an ops-first reply below; copying Monica and Rishi for implementation and SLA angles.

Operational suggestions (initial proposal):
- Primary region: us-west-2 for latency. Secondary (fallback): eu-west-1 as you suggested.
- GPU family: A100s if you need FP16 fidelity; we can also support L4s for cost-optimized quantized pipelines if model accuracy allows.
- Pool sizing: recommend initial reserved pool with ~16 GPUs (A100) sized to cover ~120 concurrent heavy requests + small buffer. This maps to expected baseline cost and predictable throughput.
- Burst policy: continuous autoscaling backed by queue-based scaling up to a burst cap of 3x reserved (i.e., up to 48 GPUs) with soft-fallback to mixed-class instances (A100 + L4) for transient peaks. Bursts beyond cap will route to thin-hosted fallback model (lower-cost) with tenant-visible routing note.
- Autoscale triggers: token-queue length > 75% for 60s and increasing CPU/KV cache miss rate. Downscale after sustained < 40% utilization for 5m.

Open items for your infra/procurement:
1) Are A100s acceptable price-wise? If not, we can design a quantized L4-first plan.
2) Any regulatory constraint requiring EU-only data residency for subset of traffic?
3) Do you want an initial canary cutover (10%) before full pool cutover? Our recommended timeline includes a 72-hour canary window.

I'll schedule a short technical kickoff once we confirm GPU family and burst cap.

—Jonas
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Malik <sara@helixai.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-17 08:27 -0700
Subject: Re: HelixAI: initial capacity needs and rollout preferences

Hi Sara — short note from the CS/implementation side. Appreciate the traffic sample; a couple clarifying points so we can lock the activation playbook:

- Expected model size and KV-caching behavior? Large context models increase memory/kvcosts, which affects pool density. If you have a baseline token-latency SLO (e.g., p95 < 220ms), call that out.
- Procurement: we typically ask for a 30-day committed window for Dedicated so we can align reserved capacity. Is Helix able to commit initially for 1-3 months? We can start with a smaller commit and scale to steady state.
- Ops readiness: we propose the following activation sequence: 1) Provision reserved pool in us-west-2, 2) Smoke test with synthetic traffic, 3) 10% canary for 72 hours, 4) Gradual ramp to 100% with burst enabled.

I'll draft a short mutual action plan (MAP) and share a HubSpot record link. If Rishi can confirm SLA targets (credits/latency), I'll include those in the MAP.

—Monica
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Malik <sara@helixai.com>
Date: 2027-05-18 10:45 -0700
Subject: Re: HelixAI: initial capacity needs and rollout preferences

On Tue, May 16, 2027 at 11:03 AM Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai> wrote:
> - Burst policy: continuous autoscaling backed by queue-based scaling up to a burst cap of 3x reserved (i.e., up to 48 GPUs) with soft-fallback to mixed-class instances (A100 + L4) for transient peaks.
>
Agree with Jonas' approach but adding SLA and billing guardrails:
- SLA: target p95 latency 250ms for production routes (we can tighten if models/profiles allow). Credits for sustained outages (>3m) are standard per contract; for large burst-induced degradation we'll apply a graduated credit scale.
- Billing: bursts beyond reserved capacity billed at burst rate (higher unit price). We'll include a monthly burst-usage cap alert that will notify your infra and our CS if usage exceeds 20% of committed capacity.
- Operational guard: if bursts exceed 2 consecutive days beyond cap more than twice in a 30-day window, we trigger a capacity review and propose increasing reserved commit.

I'll prepare the MAP SLA paragraph and share it in the hubspot record.

—Rishi
Director, Implementation Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Sara Malik <sara@helixai.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-22 15:03 -0700
Subject: Re: HelixAI: initial capacity needs and rollout preferences

Thanks everyone — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. Confirming: HelixAI approves the A100 reservation for initial pool (16 GPUs), burst cap at 3x for first 30 days, 10% canary for 72 hours, us-west-2 primary with eu-west-1 fallback. Procurement is comfortable with a 30-day committed window to start.

Action items on our side:
- I will upload final traffic profile to the Drive link and loop infra@helixai.com for a short security/egress check.
- Tom will accept the MAP in HubSpot once you push the draft.

Please go ahead and create the HubSpot MAP and the onboarding kickoff invite (30–45 minutes) for next week. We prefer Wed or Thu mornings (PST).

—Sara
Program Manager, HelixAI
